is_anopheles.evidence: The paper focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.s. (page 4, line 41).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports on Vgsc-L995F, Vgsc-L995S, Cyp6aa/p gene cluster CNVs, Cyp9k1 CNVs, and Gste2 (page 4, lines 48-54; page 15, lines 281-295; page 16, lines 304-316; page 17, lines 329-337; page 17, lines 348-351).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides diplotype clustering figures (Figures 5, 6, 7, 9) and discusses allele sharing and CNV frequencies across populations, with sample sizes provided in Table S1 (page 34).

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses 913 field-collected Anopheles gambiae s.s. mosquitoes from Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, and the DRC (page 6, lines 133-136; page 7, lines 137-141; Table S1, page 34).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study analyzing whole-genome sequence data of field-collected mosquitoes (page 6, lines 125-129).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data at the regional/district level, e.g., Benishangul-Gumuz and Gambella in Ethiopia, and various regions in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, and the DRC (Table S1, page 34).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study provides specific collection years and months for all cohorts in Table S1 (page 34).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper states it uses data from the Ag1000G project and new collections from 2023 (page 6, lines 133-136; page 7, lines 137-142). While it uses public data, it is a primary analysis of these combined datasets.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including sample sizes and locations, are provided in the main text and supplementary tables.

assessment.summary: This study analyzes the genomic connectivity and adaptive gene flow of Anopheles gambiae s.s. across East and Central Africa using whole-genome sequencing data from 913 field-collected mosquitoes. It investigates insecticide resistance markers (Vgsc, Cyp6aa/p, Cyp9k1, Gste2) and finds that while metabolic resistance markers mirror genome-wide connectivity, target-site mutations like Vgsc-L995F show restricted geographical patterns, highlighting Ethiopia as a potential 'melting pot' for resistance alleles.
